question: What are the finger like projections that increase the area of absorption of the small intestine called?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Villi__**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__** 

__
 
• ** Intestinal Villi** are small, finger-like projections that extend into the** lumen** of the small intestine.

 
 
• The inner lining of the small intestine has many finger-like projections called **villi**.
 
• Each villus is covered by a layer of epithelium and contains blood vessels and lymphatic vessels.
 
• Villi increase the surface area of the small intestine to absorb** nutrients**.
 
• Each Villus is approximately** 0.5-1.6** mm in length.
 
• It also helps the intestine to move food along the digestive pathways.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Sphincters: A ring-shaped muscle that relaxes or tightens to open or close a passage or opening in the body. Examples are the anal sphincter (around the opening of the anus) and the pyloric sphincter (at the lower opening of the stomach).
 
• Glands: An organ that makes one or more substances, such as hormones, digestive juices, sweat, tears, saliva, or milk.
 
• Cilia: They are small, slender, hair-like structures present on the surface of all mammalian cells. They are primitive in nature and could be single or many. Cilia play a major role in locomotion.
